Pod disruption budgets explained

A pod disruption budget limits how many pods of a replicated application can be down at the same time because of voluntary disruptions, such as a node drain during a cluster upgrade.

You set either minAvailable or maxUnavailable. The eviction API refuses an eviction that would violate the budget, so a drain waits until enough replicas are ready again elsewhere.

When budgets do not apply

Involuntary disruptions, such as a kernel panic or a node losing power, are not prevented by a budget, but they do count against it. Read the upstream reference for the full field list.
